attributes.nuance_translation: A phrase used when a specific event is coming, or has come to be a certain way.

attributes.body:
This grammar point is a combination of the conjunction particle て, and the verb 来（く）る 'to come'. To use this grammar point, you will need to attach て to any verb, and then follow it with くる. This nuance is usually that '(A) happened, and then came', or 'will happen, and then come'. In other words, it will depend on whether くる is in present, or past tense.

てくる can be used when representing time, or when representing a physical place. When representing a physical place, it is more likely that the kanji structure, 来（く）る will be used. However, this is not a set rule, and depends on the writer.

When used in relation to time, the nuance is usually that something has already come to pass, or will start to happen from now.

This is the opposite of ていく, which indicates that something will change from the way that it is now, or will continue progressing in a certain way.

Fun Fact

When compared to English, てくる is very similar to the phrase 'to have come to (A)', in relation to time. This means that it focuses on the fact that the speaker will 'become (A)', should things continue in a specific way. In practice though, it is used like 'gotten' in most situations.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Difference between -ていく and -てくる
How to use 〜ていく + 〜てくる
Using motion verbs （行く、来る） with the te-form

attributes.body: てくる and ていく combine the て-form of a verb with 来る or 行く to express movement or change over time. てくる suggests movement toward the speaker or a change that started in the past and leads up to now. ていく implies movement away from the speaker or a change that begins now and continues into the future.

attributes.body: ばかりだ attaches to the dictionary (non-past) form of a verb and is used to show that an action, often a negative one, keeps happening or is the only thing happening. In contrast, てくる combines the て-form of a verb with くる to describe an action that began in the past and has continued to the present. Unlike ばかりだ, てくる can be used for both positive and negative situations.

attributes.body: Both つづける and てくる can show the progression of an action over time. つづける attaches to the verb stem and focuses on the continuation of the action itself. てくる uses the て-form and emphasizes that the action started in the past and has continued up to the present.

attributes.body: The verb くる commonly expresses movement toward the speaker, similar to the English 'come.' When combined with the て form of a verb, it can be used literally (e.g., 持ってくる = 'bring') or figuratively to express progression or change over time, like the English 'come to be' (e.g., 雨が降ってくる = 'it will come to rain').

second_relatable.title: てくる
second_relatable.meaning: To come to, To become, To continue, To be starting to, Has been ~ing

attributes.body: Both ～になる／～くなる and てくる describe changes in state but differ in usage. ～になる／～くなる are used with nouns and adjectives to show something becoming a certain condition. てくる, used with verbs, suggests a gradual change over time. They can also be combined. For example, 面白くなってきた means 'It gradually became interesting.'
